Paragraph:
Translation: That is the way of the spiritual and godly life, after attaining which a man is not bewildered. Being so situated, even at the hour of death, one can enter into the kingdom of God.

Purport (Excerpt): ...brahmi sthitih means 'not on the platform of material activities.' ...Attainment of Krsna consciousness even during this life is immediate attainment of Brahman... Srila Bhaktivinode Thakur has summarized this Second Chapter... as being the contents for the whole text.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Concluding the foundational chapter of the Bhagavad Gita and addressing the ultimate transition of human life: death.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna summarizes this entire self-realized state as *Brahmi Sthitih* (being situated in the Absolute). Once attained, confusion and delusion evaporate permanently. Even if achieved in life's final moments, it grants ultimate liberation (Brahma-nirvana).
Outcome/Resolution: Chapter 2 concludes with a complete blueprint of soul identity, mental control, and ultimate liberation, leaving Arjuna equipped to face life and death without fear.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Existential Security: Standing firm in ultimate reality beyond material confusion
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Overcoming the Fear of Death: Maintaining composure and clarity during life's final transition
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Permanence of Enlightenment: Reaching a state of clarity where delusion can never return

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Brahmi sthitih (Established in the spiritual/Absolute state)
Brahma-nirvana (Liberation into the spiritual realm/extinction of material existence)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This verse concludes Chapter 2 by defining *Brahmi Sthitih*—the divine state of consciousness. Reaching this state eliminates material delusion forever. Even if one surrenders to Lord Krishna right at the final breath (as King Khatvanga did), material bondage ends and they enter the eternal spiritual kingdom.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: The ultimate test of any psychological framework is how it handles mortality. *Brahmi Sthitih* represents absolute existential clarity. When a person knows who they are beyond physical matter, even the final crisis of death loses its power to terrify or bewilder. This state provides ultimate peace, grounding, and freedom from existential anxiety.
